==English==
{{wp}}

===Etymology===
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:space<ety:bor<xno:space<ety:from<fro:espace>>>>|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|space}}, from {{der|en|xno|space}}, variant of {{m|fro|espace}}, {{m|fro|espas}}, ''et al.''; and {{m|fro|spaze}}, variant of {{m|fro|espace}}, from {{der|en|la|spatium}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*(s)peh₂-||to stretch, to pull}}. Partially displaced native {{ncog|ang|rum}}, whence {{w|Modern English}} {{m|en|room}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{enPR|spās}}, {{IPA|en|/speɪs/}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-space.ogg|a=US}}
* {{hyphenation|en|space}}
* {{rhymes|en|eɪs|s=1}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun|~}}

# {{lb|en|heading}} ''Unlimited or generalized extent, physical or otherwise.''
## The [[distance]] between [[object]]s. {{defdate|from 14<sup>th</sup>c.}}
##: {{syn|en|break|gap|Thesaurus:interspace}}
##* {{RQ:Shakespeare Antony and Cleopatra|II|iii|347|2|But neere him, thy Angell / Becomes a feare: as being o're-powr'd, therefore / Make '''ſpace''' enough betweene you.}}
##* {{RQ:Guardian|url=http://www.theguardian.com/travel/2001/nov/03/russia.moscow.guardiansaturdaytravelsection|title=Russian around|date=2001-11-03|author=Sam Wollaston|passage=Which means that for every car there was 10 years ago, there are now 40. Which means - and this is my own, not totally scientific, calculation - that the '''space''' between cars on the roads in 1991 was roughly 39 car lengths, because today there is no '''space''' at all.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261025173209/https://www.theguardian.com/travel/2001/nov/03/russia.moscow.guardiansaturdaytravelsection|archivedate=25 October 2026}}
## A physical [[extent]] across two or three dimensions (sometimes {{m|en|for}} or ''to do'' something). {{defdate|from 14<sup>th</sup>c.}}
##: {{syn|en|area|volume}}
##* {{RQ:Shakespeare Hamlet|II|iii|364|1|O God, I could be bounded in a nutſhell, and / count my ſelfe a King of infinite '''ſpace'''; were it not that / I haue bad dreames.}}
##* {{RQ:Guardian|url=http://www.theguardian.com/lifeandstyle/2007/may/12/homes|title=Lost and found - an artist's voyage from city to country|date=2007-05-12|author=Dominic Bradbury|passage=They also wanted a larger garden and more '''space''' for home working.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261027112207/https://www.theguardian.com/lifeandstyle/2007/may/12/homes|archivedate=27 October 2026}}
## A physical [[extent]] in all directions, seen as an attribute of the [[universe]] (now usually considered as a part of [[space-time]]), or a mathematical model of this. {{defdate|from 17<sup>th</sup>c.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1656|author=w:Thomas Hobbes|title=Elements of Philosophy|section=II
|passage='''Space''' is the Phantasme of a Thing existing without the Mind simply.}}
##* {{quote-journal|en|year=1880|journal=w:Popular Science|month=August
|passage=These are not questions which can be decided by reference to our '''space''' intuitions, for our intuitions are confined to Euclidean '''space''', and even there are insufficient, approximative.}}
##* {{quote-journal|en|date=15 April 2007|author=Anushka Asthana; David Smith|journal=w:The Observer
|passage=The early results from Gravity Probe B, one of Nasa's most complicated satellites, confirmed yesterday 'to a precision of better than 1 per cent' the assertion Einstein made 90 years ago - that an object such as the Earth does indeed distort the fabric of '''space''' and time.}}
## The near-[[vacuum]] in which [[planet]]s, [[star]]s and other celestial objects are situated; the [[universe]] beyond the earth's atmosphere. {{defdate|from 17<sup>th</sup>c.}}
##: {{syn|en|outer space}}
##: {{ux|en|the first man in '''space'''}}
##* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Lost|book=VII|page=188|lines=86–90|passage=How firſt began this Heav'n which we behold / Diſtant ſo high, with moving Fires adornd / Innumerable, and this which yeelds or fills / All '''ſpace''', the ambient Aire wide interfus'd / Imbracing round this florid Earth, {{...}}|year=1873}}
##* {{RQ:Wells First Men in the Moon|passage=After all, to go into outer '''space''' is not so much worse, if at all, than a polar expedition.}}
##* {{RQ:Guardian|url=http://www.theguardian.com/science/2010/aug/09/stephen-hawking-human-race-colonise-space|title=Stephen Hawking: mankind must colonise space or die out|date=2010-08-09|quotee=w:Stephen Hawking|passage=The human race must colonise '''space''' within the next two centuries or it will become extinct, Stephen Hawking warned today.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261019125348/https://www.theguardian.com/science/2010/aug/09/stephen-hawking-human-race-colonise-space|archivedate=19 October 2026}}
## The physical and psychological area one needs within which to live or operate; [[personal]] [[freedom]]. {{defdate|from 20<sup>th</sup>c.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1996|author=Linda Brodkey|title=Writing Permitted in Designated Areas Only
|passage=Around the time of my parents' divorce, I learned that reading could also give me '''space'''.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=2008|author=Jimmy Treigle|title=Walking on Water
|passage="I care about you Billy, whether you believe it or not; but right now I need my '''space'''."}}
# {{lb|en|heading}} ''Of time.''
## {{lb|en|now|rare|archaic}} [[free time|Free time]]; [[leisure]], [[opportunity]]. {{defdate|from 14<sup>th</sup>c.}}
##: {{syn|en|leisure time|spare time}}
##* {{RQ:Shakespeare All's Well|IV|i|245|2|Come on, thou are granted '''ſpace'''.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1793|author={{w|Henry Boyd (translator)|Henry Boyd}}|chapter=The Royal Message|page=408|title=Poems|publisher=Graisberry and Campbell|location=Dublin|url=https://www.google.co.nz/books/edition/Poems_chiefly_dramatic_and_lyric_Contain/OqhfAAAAcAAJ|passage=In two days hence / The Judge of life and death aſcends his ſeat. / —This will afford him '''ſpace''' to reach the camp{{nb...}}.}}
## A specific (specified) period of [[time]]. {{defdate|from 14<sup>th</sup>c.}}
##: {{syn|en|duration|span|Thesaurus:period}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1893|author=w:Mary Eleanor Wilkins Freeman|title=Giles Corey
|passage=I pray you, sirs, to take some cheers the while I go for a moment's '''space''' to my poor afflicted child.}}
##* {{RQ:Guardian|url=http://www.theguardian.com/sport/blog/2007/oct/20/wewozntrobbed|title=We wozn't robbed!|date=2007-10-20|author=Andy Bull|passage=The match was lost, though, in the '''space''' of just twenty minutes or so.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261025173127/https://www.theguardian.com/sport/blog/2007/oct/20/wewozntrobbed|archivedate=25 October 2026}}
##* {{quote-journal|en|date=September 29, 2011|author=Jon Smith|work=BBC Sport
|title=[http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/15014632.stm Tottenham 3-1 Shamrock Rovers]
|passage=But their lead lasted just 10 minutes before Roman Pavlyuchenko and Jermain Defoe both headed home in the '''space''' of two minutes to wrestle back control.}}
## An undefined period of time (without qualifier, especially a short period); a [[while#Noun|while]]. {{defdate|from 15<sup>th</sup>c.}}
##: {{syn|en|spell|while|Thesaurus:uncertain period}}
##* {{RQ:Wodehouse Inimitable Jeeves|passage=Even Comrade Butt cast off his gloom for a '''space''' and immersed his whole being in scrambled eggs.}}
# {{lb|en|heading}} ''A bounded or specific extent, physical or otherwise.''
## A (chiefly empty) area or volume with set [[limit]]s or [[boundaries]]; {{lb|en|architecture}} such a space inside or outside a building, often with a specified use. {{defdate|from 14<sup>th</sup>c.}}
##: {{ux|en|exhibition '''space'''; public '''space'''; the '''space''' is light-filled}}
##* {{RQ:Hough Purchase Price|chapter=II|passage=Carried somehow, somewhither, for some reason, on these surging floods, were these travelers,{{nb...}}. Even such a boat as the ''Mount Vernon'' offered a total deck '''space''' so cramped as to leave secrecy or privacy well out of the question, even had the motley and democratic assemblage of passengers been disposed to accord either.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=2000|author=Ziba Mir-Hosseini|title=Islam and Gender
|passage=The street door was open, and we entered a narrow '''space''' with washing facilities, curtained off from the courtyard.}}
##* {{RQ:Guardian|url=http://www.theguardian.com/artanddesign/2012/jul/16/tate-modern-tanks-live-art|title=Tate Modern unlocks Tanks – and introduces live art into mainstream|date=2012-07-16|author=Charlotte Higgins|passage=Converted from vast chambers beneath the old Bankside Power Station which once held a million gallons of oil, the new public areas consist of two large circular '''spaces''' for performances and film installations, plus a warren of smaller rooms.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261025173117/https://www.theguardian.com/artanddesign/2012/jul/16/tate-modern-tanks-live-art|archivedate=25 October 2026}}
## {{lb|en|music}} A position on the [[staff]] or [[stave]] bounded by lines. {{defdate|from 15<sup>th</sup>c.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1849|author=Guillaume Louis Bocquillon-Wilhem|translator=w:John Pyke Hullah|title=Wilhelm's Method of Teaching Singing
|passage=The note next above Sol is La; La, therefore, stands in the 2nd '''space'''; Si, on the 3rd line, &c.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1990|author=Sammy Nzioki|title=Music Time
|passage=The lines and '''spaces''' of the staff are named according to the first seven letters of the alphabet, that is, A B C D E F G.}}
## A [[gap]] in [[text]] between [[word]]s, [[line]]s etc., or a digital character used to create such a gap. {{defdate|from 16<sup>th</sup>c.}}
##: {{syn|en|blank|gap|whitespace<q:graphic design>}}
##: {{hyper|en|punctuation mark}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1992|author=Sam H Ham|title=Environmental Interpretation
|passage=According to experts, a single line of text should rarely exceed about 50 characters (including letters and all the '''spaces''' between words).}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=2005|author=Dr BR Kishore|title=Dynamic Business Letter Writing
|passage=It should be typed a '''space''' below the salutation : Dear Sir, Subject : Replacement of defective items.}}
## {{lb|en|metal type}} A piece of metal [[type]] used to separate [[words]], [[cast]] lower than other type so as not to take ink, especially one that is narrower than one [[en]] (compare ''[[quad]]''). {{defdate|from 17<sup>th</sup>c.}}
##: {{syn|en|quad|quadrat}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1683|author=w:Joseph Moxon|title=Mechanick Exercises: Or, the Doctrine of Handy-Works. Applied to the art of Printing.|volume=2|url=http://books.google.com/books?id=npQtAAAAYAAJ&pg=PA240&q=space+OR+spaces#PPA240,M1|pages=240–1
|passage=If it be only a ''Single Letter'' or two that drops, he thruſts the end of his ''Bodkin'' between every ''Letter'' of that Word, till he comes to a '''''Space''''': and then perhaps by forcing thoſe ''Letters'' closer, he may have room to put in another '''''Space''''' or a ''Thin '''Space'''''; which if he cannot do, and he finds the '''''Space''''' ſtand ''Looſe'' in the ''Form''; he with the ''Point'' of his ''Bodkin'' picks the '''''Space''''' up and bows it a little; which bowing makes the ''Letters'' on each ſide of the '''''Space''''' keep their parallel diſtance; for by its Spring it thruſts the ''Letters'' that were cloſed with the end of the ''Bodkin'' to their adjunct ''Letters'', that needed no cloſing.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1979|author=Marshall Lee|title=Bookmaking|pageurl=http://books.google.com/books?id=yiSeCZTFAtQC|page=110
|passage=Horizontal spacing is further divided into multiples and fractions of the em. The multiples are called ''quads''. The fractions are called '''''spaces'''''.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=2005|author=Phil Baines; Andrew Haslam|title=Type & Typography|edition=2nd|pageurl=http://books.google.com/books?id=rs6gyb2hPF4C|page=91
|passage=Other larger '''spaces''' – known as quads – were used to space out lines.}}
## A [[gap]]; an empty place. {{defdate|from 17<sup>th</sup>c.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=2004|editor=Harry M Benshoff|title=Queer Cinéma
|passage=Mainstream Hollywood would not cater to the taste for sexual sensation, which left a '''space''' for B-movies, including noir.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=2009|author=Barbara L. Lev|title=From Pink to Green
|passage=A horizontal scar filled the '''space''' on her chest where her right breast used to be.}}
## {{lb|en|geometry}} A [[set]] of [[point]]s, each of which is [[unique]]ly specified by a number (the [[dimensionality]]) of [[coordinate]]s.
## {{lb|en|countable|mathematics}} A [[generalized]] [[construct]] or [[set]] whose members have some property in common; typically there will be a geometric metaphor allowing these members to be viewed as “points”. Often used with a restricting modifier describing the members (e.g. ''[[vector space]]''), or indicating the inventor of the construct (e.g. ''[[Hilbert space]]''). {{defdate|from 20<sup>th</sup>c.}}
##: {{ux|en|Functional analysis is best approached through a sound knowledge of Hilbert '''space''' theory.}}
## {{lb|en|countable|figuratively}} A [[field]], [[area]], or [[sphere]] of activity or endeavour.
##: {{ux|en|innovation in the browser '''space'''}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=2019|author=Ryan Derousseau|title=The Everything Guide to Investing in Cryptocurrency{{...|: From Bitcoin to Ripple, the Safe and Secure Way to Buy, Trade, and Mine Digital Currencies}}|publisher=Simon and Schuster|isbn=9781507209332|page=269|pageurl=https://books.google.com/books?id=9DxqDwAAQBAJ&pg=PA269&dq=%22crypto+space%22&hl=&cd=6&source=gbs_api#v=onepage&q=%22crypto%20space%22&f=false|text=CNBC has shown a greater commitment to the crypto '''space''' than most other mainstream outlets, providing daily updates on bitcoin or other very large cryptocurrencies.}}
## Anything analogous to a physical space in which one can interact, such as an [[online]] [[chat room]].
##* {{quote-book|en|year=2007|author=Jacob van Kokswijk|title=Digital Ego: Social and Legal Aspects of Virtual Identity|page=88
|passage=Communication in Internet chat '''spaces''' allows participants to communicate so freely in the relative safety of anonymity that they forget their privacy.}}
